models.purpose: Specify the two phases of security screening as queues in series.
models.summary: Phase 1 is an M/M/c queue with service rate 0.09465 per second, estimated after a two-officer t-test (1.375 against 2.145 at 5 percent) failed to reject equal means. Phase 2 is an M/E_k/c queue with k equal to 4 and service rate 0.0357. Because the phases are in series the arrival rate of the second equals the service rate of the first. Arrival rates are 0.077244 regular and 0.10882016 pre-check, both kept after chi-squared tests of 15.898 and 15.599 against 16.919.

variables.definition: arrival rate at the document check
service rate of one document officer, 0.09465
service rate of one scan lane, 0.0357
Erlang type of the scan service, fixed at 4
expected total waiting time across both phases

governing_equations.purpose: arrival rate of the second phase equals service rate of the first

objectives: Specify the two phases of security screening as queues in series.
constraints: service rate is the same for every officer

parameter_estimation.method: maximum likelihood for the exponential rate, moment fit for the Erlang order

steps: link the phases by the series equality

assumptions: passengers always join the shortest queue
strengths: every parameter is estimated from the given sheet or from named public data
limitations: the printed expectation of the Erlang distribution says alpha, while the variance says alpha times beta squared, which is inconsistent with a mean of alpha beta
missing_details: the chi-squared classes for the pre-check fit are not tabulated

models.purpose: Build the hourly passenger flow by summing one normal distribution per flight.
models.summary: Each flight at O'Hare on 18 January 2017 is given a normal arrival centered two hours before departure, with the three-sigma point half an hour before departure, and a capacity of 189 taken from the Boeing 737-800. Summing the densities gives a flow that peaks near 9:30. Recommending an earlier arrival cuts the mean wait from about 83 seconds at 90 minutes early to 26.0189 seconds at 120 minutes early.

variables.definition: mean minutes before departure that passengers arrive
spread of arrival times for one flight

governing_equations.purpose: one normal distribution per flight, centered two hours early

objectives: Build the hourly passenger flow by summing one normal distribution per flight.

parameter_estimation.method: center taken from the TSA recommendation, capacity from the aircraft type

assumptions: almost everyone arrives at least half an hour early

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the flow is plotted for one day but not checked against counted arrivals

strengths: every parameter is estimated from the given sheet or from named public data
limitations: the capacity of 189 is the top of a stated range of 104 to 189, not a measured load
missing_details: the chi-squared classes for the pre-check fit are not tabulated

models.purpose: Mix first in first served with departure priority through one factor.
models.summary: Priority of a waiting passenger is alpha times departure time plus one minus alpha times arrival time. At 721 to 723 passengers per hour, missed flights over ten experiments average 281.2 under first in first served, 71.3 at alpha 0.5, and 9.4 under strict priority. Remaining-time variance falls from 6.8787 million to 5.1711 million to 3.9684 million, while the means stay near 6900.

variables.definition: weight on departure time, between 0 and 1
time the passenger reached the checkpoint
passengers who miss their flight under the discipline

governing_equations.purpose: priority as a convex mix of departure time and arrival time

objectives: Mix first in first served with departure priority through one factor.
assumptions: a passenger's priority depends only on arrival time and departure time

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: ten runs at each of three policies, means reported

strengths: every parameter is estimated from the given sheet or from named public data
limitations: the two flow rates, 723 and 721 passengers per hour, are not reconciled
missing_details: the chi-squared classes for the pre-check fit are not tabulated
